headline: iPhone and iPad integration lands, and macOS gains a selectable Metal renderer
summary: iPhone and iPad gained the shared launcher, local disc import and native platform support (#375, #376, #377). macOS players can select Metal in Advanced settings, with Enhanced graphics still using Vulkan (#370, #382). Going Commando's PAL and USA v2.00 ports now enter levels after headless checks, with USA v2.00's Oozla and Aranos openings fixed too (#401, #405). Mod SDK 1.14.1 and 1.14.2 were released as Going Commando gained multiplayer support and item-randomizer hook points (#385, #386, #387, #390).
highlights: Desktop players can choose a save folder, closing #332 (#388). Individual Steam game entries gain their own artwork and direct launch options, closing #333 (#389).
Touch controls gain Going Commando-specific actions, an O button for prompts such as manual saving, and a large movie-skip button (#395, #402, #404).
The launcher and in-game menu adopt the site's gold look, with optional game colours. Gruvbox settings fall back to OpenRAC after that theme's removal (#339, #393, #396).
#391 reports Novalis Enhanced lighting preparation falling from 184 to 64 seconds with new defaults. Its level 9 tests ran 2.8 times faster with BC6H and 2.5 times faster with ASTC.
Pinned decompilation submodules replace copied source trees, accounting for most of the day's four million deleted lines. Upstreamed patches are then removed from OpenRAC (#371, #408).
Hrugis Cloud's giant orange squares are fixed (#392). Up Your Arsenal's PAL disc gains recognition and build support (#381). Enhanced bloom remains an unmerged proposal (#407).
